text:
sam-recruiter: Quick sync 026 hire: candidate is Canadian, currently on TN, wants to start working remotely from Toronto and then move to US on H-1B if selected in cap. Proposed US start 2027-10-01. Can we proceed and what operational steps do we need?

ina-peopleops: Yes we can. Main things: cross-border payroll implications while in Canada, benefits eligibility timing, and immigration filing ownership. Are they joining the US entity?

sam-recruiter: Yes, employed by Redwood US. They prefer USD pay while in Canada.

mike-legal: Immigration note: we can register them for the H-1B cap. If selected, change-of-status (COS) vs consular processing depends on travel and prior visa status. If they stay in Canada until COS effective date there's less risk. If they enter US on TN then switch, travel rules get trickier.

imm-bot: Upload checklist: passport, TN approval (if currently on TN), Canadian proof of residence, signed offer, H-1B questionnaire, prior US visas. Please use secure intake.

tara-payroll: Payroll constraints: paying an employee in USD while they reside in Canada triggers Canadian payroll/tax obligations. Options: 1) set up Canadian payroll (vendor) and remit Canadian taxes, 2) treat as contractor (not preferred), 3) set up a payroll service to handle cross-border withholding. We need candidate's expected remote duration to size the solution.

ina-peopleops: If duration remote-from-Canada is <90 days, we might treat it as business travel, but that depends on their work pattern. We should get an expected relocation date. Also confirm whether they will have dependents moving later.

sam-recruiter: Candidate expects to stay in Canada until H-1B COS date (if selected). No dependents moving initially.

mike-legal: Good. That simplifies things. We should still budget for a cross-border payroll vendor for the interim period. Legal recommends we cover standard H-1B legal fees; premium processing decision to be made case-by-case.

tara-payroll: Action items for recruiter: confirm pay currency, confirm remote duration, collect Canadian SIN and any US SSN, and ask candidate if they want bridging health while in Canada.

ina-peopleops: Benefits: we can queue enrollment now and set effective date to US start. Non-US residence = ineligible for US-sourced medical until they have US address and BR. We can offer a temporary monthly stipend for private coverage while in Canada.

sam-recruiter: Candidate asked who pays for bridging coverage and for premium processing. Any guidance?

mike-legal: Company pays standard immigration legal fees and filing fees. Premium processing yes for mission-critical hires, approved by hiring manager and People Ops. Bridging health stipend is handled as a one-time relocation/misc stipend; confirm budget with finance.

imm-bot: Reminder: once candidate accepts, please request CoS docs (if applicable), and upload scans at least 10 business days before any targeted start.

tara-payroll: We'll prepare a checklist to stand up the temporary payroll vendor; need GL codes and manager approval. Expect ~2 weeks lead time.

sam-recruiter: I'll confirm currency and duration today and upload docs. Thanks all :pray:
